content:
The new Apple TV 4K has been a long time coming, originally expected to launch last fall. But now that Siri AI is finally ready, all signs point to the new Apple TV 4K making its debut, possibly at the September 9 event. Here's what's been rumored so far.

#1: Siri Remote Refresh

While no details have leaked, Apple is reportedly preparing an updated Siri Remote for the new Apple TV 4K.

Code from one of the macOS 26.7 builds appears to confirm the existence of a next-generation Siri Remote. Ahead of this leak, Mark Gurman had already reported that a "tweaked Apple TV remote" could arrive alongside the new hardware.

It doesn't look like there will be major changes, but hopefully at least a second-generation ultra-wideband chip will be added for Precision Finding support.

#2: Siri AI and More Apple Intelligence Features

Siri AI is expected to be the main marketing focus for the new Apple TV and other new home products.

Apple has yet to announce whether the new assistant will land on Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But there's growing evidence that tvOS 27 will include Siri AI, and there's a good chance it will only support the new hardware.

Other Apple Intelligence features are likely to be added, such as a more powerful search experience.

#3: Next-Generation A-Series Chip

The current Apple TV uses the A15 Bionic chip, first introduced in 2021. The good news is that the new model is expected to deliver a significant performance boost.

The new A-series chip will be more powerful and support various AI features.

Rumors have suggested it could be the A17 Pro or A18 chip. But most of those reports came before the Siri AI rollout. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple instead equipped it with a more powerful A19 or A20 chip.

#4: N1 Wireless Chip

From the highest-voted comment left by Doug

So, ideally, it could replace the legacy HomePod device to support Siri AI.

Second, it should have built-in microphones so users can issue Siri AI commands without having to hold the remote.

Finally, it should deliver the universal TV remote functionality it should have had all along (but was blocked by partners like Netflix), so I can search for new shows across all services, including cable providers.

Netflix's library data is public, so Siri AI could search across all the media I have access to. Apple TV should be that universal set-top box.

Also, AirPlay should support syncing across multiple HomePods for a true home theater setup. That means user-tunable Atmos sound.

The N1 wireless chip, first adopted in the iPhone 17, is also rumored to be included in the new Apple TV 4K.

With the N1, the Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as Thread networking support.

By comparison, the existing Apple TV hardware, now four years old, only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features are you hoping to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
